## alias

One row per name that refers to a relying party. The same service is called
different things in different systems, and this table maps each of those strings
back to a single `rp_id`.

Use it to join tables that have no shared service identifier, such as
`ibm_verify.app_login_counts.application_name` and the `rp_name` breakdown in the
Google Analytics funnel tables.

`Keywords`: Relying party, RP, alias, application name, crosswalk, lookup, join

### Provenance

Maintained by hand in the same
[CanadaLogin Relying Parties Google Sheet](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/11czXAX6mTxZbbcH_XbFmI-TSoSTc2M5FXUp9teGw1D0/edit?gid=0#gid=0)
as [`rp.service`](#service), read every weekday by the same Lambda and written as a
single Parquet file. Not partitioned, overwritten in place, current state only.

* **Updated**: Weekdays, at 06:00 ET
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Colin Douglas](mailto:colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://canadalogin-reporting-transformed/rp/alias/`

### Fields

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alias` | `varchar` | The string that refers to the service, exactly as the source system writes it. |
| `rp_id` | `bigint` | The relying party this alias refers to. Joins to `rp.service.rp_id`. |
| `source` | `varchar` | Where the alias was first encountered, one of `IBM Verify` or `Google Analytics`. Record keeping only, see the note below. |
| `fetched_at` | `timestamp(3)` | When the Lambda last read the source sheet, in UTC. |

### Notes

**Join on `alias` alone. Do not filter on `source`.** `source` records where the
name was first seen, not which system the name belongs to. Filtering by it before
joining will silently drop matches for any alias that turns up in both systems.

**One service, several aliases.** A service has as many rows here as it has names. For 
example, `MyCGC` is `MyCGC` in Google Analytics but both `MyCGC - CGC - .NET - Prod` and
`MyCGC - CGC - Power Pages - Prod` in IBM Verify. Joining a fact table through
this lookup is a many-to-one join, so aggregate after the join, not before.

**Not every string in the analytics tables is an alias.** The `rp_name` breakdown
in the Google Analytics funnel tables also contains `RESERVED_TOTAL` (the
all-services rollup), `(not set)`, and the empty string. None of these are
services, and an inner join drops them. If you are reconciling totals, exclude
`RESERVED_TOTAL` explicitly rather than relying on the join to remove it.

**Aliases are exact strings, not patterns.** They are matched literally, with no
trimming or case folding. A new application name in IBM Verify will not resolve
until it is added to the source sheet by hand.
